A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPlug research and contain readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–B. Relocated test results and renumbered appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPlug evaluations on six LaMP tasks, including validation/test results, component ablations, and history-selection experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds an analysis of PPlug performance across users with different history lengths.

M1.justification: The encoders, input-aware aggregation, two-layer projection, instruction embedding, frozen LLM, and training objective remain unchanged. The retrieval-augmented and top-K variants already appear in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LaMP-1, -2, -3, -4, -5, and -7. Test-set evaluation already appears in v1's appendix; the new history-length analysis uses existing LaMP-3 and LaMP-5 validation users.

E2.justification: v1 explicitly excludes per-user fine-tuning baselines. v2 Section 4.3 and Table 1 add FTP, per-user LoRA on FlanT5-XXL, using test results copied from Salemi and Zamani (2024) across all six tasks. This introduces a previously excluded central comparison family while retaining the existing comparators.

E3.justification: The new history-length analysis divides LaMP-3 and LaMP-5 validation users into short, medium, and long groups in a 1:1:1 ratio, evaluating RMSE and ROUGE-1 respectively. Existing splits, metrics, model configurations, and stated training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and new Table 5 examine performance across users with different amounts of history. This supplements the retained component ablations, encoder/backbone comparisons, retrieval integration, and top-K history-selection analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, performance confidence intervals, or significance-test procedures. The dataset-length summary statistics remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds FTP test scores and history-group results, including LaMP-3 RMSE of 0.548/0.531/0.522 for short/medium/long histories. PPlug's validation LaMP-7 ROUGE-1 changes from 0.536 to 0.534 in Tables 1–2, matching the unchanged detailed Table 8. Existing test scores move from v1 Table 7 into v2 Table 1 without numerical changes.

T1.justification: The task formulation, model equations (1–6), and appendix normalization equation (7) remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, and conclusion retain the central claims: aggregate user histories into one embedding, guide a fixed LLM efficiently, and improve personalization. The added comparisons support rather than redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 attributes FTP's limited gains to scarce per-user data and interprets Table 5 as showing effectiveness even with shorter histories. It removes v1's explanation linking especially large LaMP-2/7 gains to general style knowledge. The stated limitations and privacy argument are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link, approximate PPlug resource requirements of 100 hours and 150 GB, and test-set counts in Appendix Table 6. It removes v1's AdamW optimizer, learning rate of 1e-4, and warmup ratio of 0.05; this is lost documentation, not evidence of changed optimization.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of Doddapaneni, Ning, and Hebert, distinguishing their recommendation-oriented personalization from PPlug. It revises HYDRA's description from user clustering to per-user language heads and adds the source for FTP comparisons. These extend the existing positioning without fundamentally reframing it.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language edits, revises portions of the baseline/results discussion, updates affiliations and contacts, and adds acknowledgements. The main section structure remains intact; appendix subsections are renumbered after test results move into the main text.

P2.justification: Table 1 combines v1's validation and appendix test tables, adding split labels and an FTP column. v2 adds history-length Table 5 and a test-count column to the dataset table. Figures 1–4 retain their content, with limited caption, sizing, and placement changes.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the evaluation more informative by adding a clearly sourced fine-tuning comparator and reporting performance by history length. Clearer split presentation, corrected summary scores, expanded related work, and code-access information also help. These gains are partly offset by removing explicit optimizer, learning-rate, and warmup settings, which weakens reproducibility from the paper alone.
